questions.stem: When constructing the perpendicular bisector of a line segment AB using a compass, you draw arcs from both A and B. What must be true about the compass width?

options.text: It must be exactly half the length of AB
It must be more than half the length of AB
It must be exactly the length of AB
It can be any width

questions.explanation: The compass width must be more than half the length of AB so that the arcs from A and B intersect. If it is exactly half or less, the arcs will not cross.

questions.stem: What does the perpendicular bisector of a line segment create at the point where it crosses the segment?

options.text: Two 45-degree angles
Two 60-degree angles
Two 90-degree angles and two equal halves
Two unequal parts at 90 degrees

questions.explanation: A perpendicular bisector crosses the line segment at 90 degrees AND at its midpoint, creating two equal halves.

questions.stem: When constructing an angle bisector of angle ABC, arcs are drawn from B to cross BA and BC at points P and Q. Arcs are then drawn from P and Q. The line from B through the intersection of these arcs creates what?

options.text: A line perpendicular to BC
Two equal angles, each half of angle ABC
A line parallel to AC
A perpendicular bisector of PQ

questions.explanation: An angle bisector divides the angle into two equal parts. Each part is half the size of angle ABC.

questions.stem: To construct a triangle with sides 5 cm, 7 cm, and 9 cm, you draw the base of 9 cm first. You then set the compass to 5 cm from one end and 7 cm from the other. Where is the third vertex?

options.text: At the midpoint of the base
Where the two arcs intersect
5 cm directly above the left end of the base
Where either arc crosses the base

questions.explanation: The third vertex is at the point where the two arcs intersect. This point is exactly 5 cm from one end and 7 cm from the other, giving a triangle with the correct side lengths.

questions.stem: When constructing a perpendicular from a point P to a line L, you first draw an arc from P that crosses L at two points A and B. What do you do next?

options.text: Draw the perpendicular bisector of AB
Connect P to the midpoint of AB by eye
Measure equal distances from A and B along the line
Draw an arc from A only

questions.explanation: You construct the perpendicular bisector of AB. Since P is equidistant from A and B, P lies on the perpendicular bisector. The perpendicular bisector of AB passes through P and is perpendicular to L.
